{{nihongo|'''Omiashi Shrine'''|於美阿志神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Yamato Province]].

=== Enshrined deities ===
* Two deities, husband and wife, of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Achi no Omi}} - ancestral deities of the {{ill|Yamatonoaya clan|Q10870550|qid=Q10870550}}.

=== History ===
This area is said to have been the residence site of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Achi no Omi}}, who came to Japan in the reign of the 15th emperor, {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|Q317997|qid=Q317997}}. In the late {{ill|7th century|Q8089|qid=Q8089}}, {{ill|Hinokuma-dera|ja|檜隈寺|qid=Q11544640}} was built as the {{ill|Clan temple|Q11547815|qid=Q11547815}} of the {{ill|Yamatonoaya clan|Q10870550|qid=Q10870550}}.

Later, west of the present site across the road, this shrine was founded as the {{ill|Ujigami|Q767655|qid=Q767655}} of the Yamato-no-Aya clan, with Achi no Omi and his wife as {{ill|Saijin|Q11591100|qid=Q11591100}}{{Sfn|日本の神社研究会|2018|page=142}}, and as the guardian shrine of Hinokuma-dera.

By the {{ill|Kamakura period|Q236205|qid=Q236205}}, Hinokuma-dera was called Doko-ji, and in the {{ill|Edo period|ar|فترة إيدو|ast|Periodu Edo|az|Edo dövrü|bcl|Panahon nin Edo|be|Перыяд Эда|bg|Едо (период)|bn|এদো যুগ|bo|ཨེ་དོའི་དུས་སྐབས།|br|Marevezh Edo|ca|Període Edo|ckb|سەردەمی ئێدۆ|cs|Období Edo|cv|Эдо тапхăрĕ|da|Edo-perioden|de|Edo-Zeit|eo|Epoko de Edo|es|Período Edo|et|Edo ajastu|eu|Edo aroa|fa|دوره ادو|fi|Edo-kausi|fr|Époque d'Edo|gl|Período Edo|he|תקופת אדו|hi|एदो अवधी|hr|Edo (razdoblje)|hu|Edo-kor|id|Zaman Edo|is|Jedótímabilið|it|Periodo Edo|ja|江戸時代|jv|Jaman Édo|ko|에도 시대|lt|Edo laikotarpis|lv|Edo periods|mk|Едо (период)|mn|Эдогийн эрин|ms|Zaman Edo|nl|Edoperiode|nn|Edotida|oc|Periòde Edo|pl|Edo (okres)|pt|Período Edo|ro|Perioada Edo|ru|Период Эдо|simple|Edo period|sk|Obdobie Edo|sl|Obdobje Edo|sq|Periudha Edo|sr|Едо период|su|Période Edo|sv|Edoperioden|th|ยุคเอโดะ|tl|Panahong Edo|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Eto|tr|Edo Dönemi|uk|Період Едо|ur|ایڈو دور|uz|Edo davri|vi|Thời kỳ Edo|war|Panahon Edo|wuu|江戶時代|zh|江户时代|zh_min_nan|Edo sî-tāi|zh_yue|江戶時代|qid=Q184963}} this shrine was called Goryo Myojin.

When {{ill|Motoori Norinaga|Q384647|qid=Q384647}} visited in {{ill|1772|Q7690|qid=Q7690}} ({{ill|Meiwa|Q1146161|qid=Q1146161}} 9), only a temporary hut remained at Hinokuma-dera and old roof tiles were scattered in the precincts; Hinokuma-dera was later abolished.

In {{ill|1907|Q2048|qid=Q2048}} ({{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 40), the main hall was relocated to the former site of Hinokuma-dera.

It is also said that {{ill|Emperor Senka|ar|الإمبراطور سينكا|arz|الامبراطور سينكا|azb|سینکا (ایمپیراتور)|cs|Senka|de|Senka|es|Senka Tennō|fa|امپراتور سنکا|fi|Senka|fr|Senka|id|Kaisar Senka|it|Senka|ja|宣化天皇|ka|სენკა|ko|센카 천황|nl|Senka|pl|Senka|pt|Senka|ru|Император Сэнка|sh|Car Senka|simple|Emperor Senka|sl|Cesar Senka|sv|Senka|th|จักรพรรดิเซ็งกะ|tl|Emperador Senka|tr|Senka (imparator)|uk|Імператор Сенка|uz|Imperator Senka|vi|Thiên hoàng Senka|yo|Emperor Senka|zh|宣化天皇|zh_min_nan|Senka Thian-hông|zh_yue|宣化天皇|qid=Q329728}}'s {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Hinokuma Iorino-no-Miya}} stood in this area, though this is uncertain.

* Hinokuma-dera pagoda site - platform remains. The nearby central foundation stone is a replica.

=== Cultural properties ===
=== Important Cultural Property ===
* Omiashi Shrine stone stupa, with associated offering implements (small glass jar, qingbai lidded container, four-eared jar with lid) - the eleven-tier stone pagoda. Designated on April 5, {{ill|1909|Q2057|qid=Q2057}} ({{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 42); associated items additionally designated on June 17, {{ill|1970|Q2474|qid=Q2474}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 45)<ref>{{Cite web|和書|url= https://asukamura.jp/bunkazai/shiteibunkazai_11.html |title=Cultural Properties |publisher=Asuka Village |accessdate=2019-09-13 }}</ref>.
